title: Global slippageToleranceBps couples withdrawal slippage to deposit principal-credit: raising tolerance to clear a stuck withdrawal silently haircuts concurrent depositors' credited principal
file:line: src/concreteYieldStrategies/ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:88-93 (setSlippageTolerance, bounded only by MAX_BPS), 106-108 (_creditedPrincipal = amount*(MAX_BPS-bps)/MAX_BPS), 139 (deposit minOut), 168/225/276 (withdraw/totalWithdraw/skim minOut)
economic-mechanism: A SINGLE slippageToleranceBps governs BOTH legs: the deposit credit (_creditedPrincipal) and every swap floor (minOut on deposit/withdraw/skim/totalWithdraw). The two cannot be decoupled. If the owner raises tolerance to push a withdrawal/skim through thin AMM liquidity, every deposit that lands during the elevated window books creditedPrincipal = amount*(MAX_BPS-bps)/MAX_BPS while the FULL nominal `amount` is pulled and swapped to shares. The shortfall (amount - creditedPrincipal) is not lost from the protocol but is silently reclassified as un-attributed surplus (totalValue > totalDeposited), later skimmable to the skim recipient. At the MAX_BPS=10000 extreme the depositor is credited ZERO principal while their full deposit is converted to strategy-held surplus, and minOut=0 removes all sandwich protection on the same swap.
who-loses: Depositing authorized clients (e.g. SYA/stable-staker end-users) during an elevated-tolerance window — they permanently lose the haircut fraction of their principal claim.
who-gains: The protocol surplus pool / skim recipient (value stays inside the protocol, redistributed away from the depositor). At MAX_BPS, also MEV sandwichers via minOut=0.
preconditions: Owner raises slippageToleranceBps materially (e.g. to clear a withdrawal during volatility) AND a deposit arrives before tolerance is lowered. No third-party attacker required; the harm is the non-obvious coupling, not malice.
relation-to-changed-code/ledger: NOT diff-new (setSlippageTolerance/MAX_BPS coupling predates story-047/048; carried LOCAL-MKT-001). Requested as MR-004 economic blast-radius check. Adjacent to acknowledged M-02 NAV/slippage cluster and existing C-01 centralization triage. Non-obvious-footgun test (Law 3): a competent owner bumping tolerance to fix a withdrawal would plausibly be surprised it also halves concurrent depositors' credited principal — surprise => in-scope as operational hazard, but value-stays-in-protocol + owner-trust discount lands this Low/QA. Downstream stable-staker story-011 zero-credit guard mitigates the zero-credit extreme for depositFor users. Recommend: cap setSlippageTolerance well below MAX_BPS (e.g. <= 1000) and pause deposits before raising tolerance for an operational withdrawal.

title: story-047 pools ALL clients' set-aside buffers into one global recipient: with buffers configured on more than one client, non-recipient clients silently subsidize the recipient's beneficiary; stale NatSpec still promises a per-client dip reserve
severity-proposal: Low (owner footgun + spec drift; QA doc fix at minimum)
file:line: src/concreteYieldStrategies/ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:353-372 (_distributeBuffer: single aggregate transfer to setAsideBufferRecipient); src/AYieldStrategy.sol:51-53 (STALE NatSpec: buffer 'returned to the client... reserve to absorb below-par dips'), 318-341 (STALE AUDITOR NOTE reasons about a client redirecting buffer 'to itself'), 352-357 (setSetAsideBufferRecipient)
economic-mechanism: Pre-047 each client received its own proportional set-aside back as a dip-absorption reserve. Post-047 every surplus-bearing client's set-aside is SUMMED (totalSetAside) and sent in ONE transfer to a single global setAsideBufferRecipient. When buffers are configured on multiple clients but the recipient services only one of them (intended sink: stable-staker), the set-aside accrued from the OTHER clients' surpluses is redirected to the recipient's beneficiary — a cross-client value transfer. Conservation itself is sound (verified bufferConservation: totalSetAside <= underlyingReceived, dust favors skim recipient); the issue is distributional, not a leak.
who-loses: Any client other than the one the global recipient serves, that has a nonzero setAsideBufferSize — its stakers lose the dip reserve the in-code docs still promise. Also the skim `recipient` (its proceeds are reduced by the aggregate set-aside, same as before).
preconditions: Owner configures nonzero setAsideBufferSize on >1 client while routing to a single recipient, OR configures any buffer while relying on the stale NatSpec's per-client-reserve promise. Owner-config only; clients are protocol-owned, so no external-attacker profit and the front-run-the-skim quirk (L322-334) now only shifts value between the skim recipient and the global recipient (both protocol-owned) — story-047 actually REMOVES the old self-benefit incentive.
relation-to-changed-code/ledger: Directly story-047 (933620d). Implementation is FAITHFUL to story-047's stated intent (global redirect, plausibly the integration leg of stable-staker M-05 / ledger ss7m5/0dca43f3 pro-rata-haircut funding). The reportable residue is (a) the cross-client subsidization being a non-obvious footgun when >1 client has a buffer, and (b) the stale NatSpec/AUDITOR-NOTE (LOCAL-BASE-047-001 / MR-003) that would lead an owner to expect per-client insulation. Do NOT report the per-client->global move itself as theft (owner-intended). Hand consumer-side correctness to story-faithfulness/interaction (see ECON-005).

title: Two-phase totalWithdrawal executes the LIVE client balance, not the announced Phase-1 snapshot; story-048's 6h/72h retiming widens the announced-vs-executed drift horizon to 78h
severity-proposal: QA / Low (transparency / commitment weakening; owner-initiated, Law 3 discount)
file:line: src/AYieldStrategy.sol:822-837 (_initiateWithdrawal caches state.balance = principalOf(client) and announces it in WithdrawalInitiated), 846-860 (_executeWithdrawal forwards the cached amount), 84-86 (story-048 WAITING_PERIOD 24h->6h, EXECUTION_WINDOW 48h->72h), 414 (STALE docstring still says 24h/48h); src/concreteYieldStrategies/ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:209-240 (_totalWithdraw uses the cached `amount` only for require(>0), then sells shares proportional to LIVE clientBalances[token][client]/totalDeposited and zeroes the live balance)
economic-mechanism: Phase 1 snapshots and publicly announces the client's principal (balanceOf == principalOf). Phase 2 ignores that snapshot for sizing: it computes sharesToSell from the LIVE clientStoredBalance at execution time. If the client accrues fresh deposits between Phase 1 and Phase 2, the executed withdrawal sweeps the grown live balance without a fresh waiting period, so the executed amount can EXCEED the announced amount. story-048 shrank the community reaction window 24h->6h while widening the execution window 48h->72h, so live state can drift for up to 78h after a 6h-old announcement. Accounting itself stays correct (it zeroes exactly the live balance and decrements totalDeposited by the same), so this is a transparency/anti-rug-commitment weakening, not an over-withdraw bug.
who-loses: The 'community protection against rugpulls' commitment — observers cannot treat the announced figure as a cap on what gets migrated.
who-gains: No third party; proceeds go to owner() for manual redistribution.
preconditions: totalWithdrawal is onlyOwner; realizing the divergence requires the trusted owner to initiate it and a client to keep accepting deposits during the window. Per Law 3 the malicious-owner framing is suppressed; the residual is the non-obvious 'executes live, not announced' consequence + the silent 4x window reduction.
relation-to-changed-code/ledger: Folds PATTERN-001 (TWO-STEP-COMMIT-WINDOW). Overlaps ledger carryover L-13 (zero-snapshot, benign no-op direction); the live-balance-GREW direction plus the story-048 6h/72h retiming is the diff-relevant angle — reconcile against L-13 rather than re-report fresh. Also pairs with LOCAL-BASE-048-001 (stale 24h/48h docstring at L414 and IYieldStrategy.sol:101) and LOCAL-BASE-048-002 (security-parameter relaxation needs a story blessing). story-faithfulness should confirm story-048 covers the 6h relaxation and no downstream consumer (stable-staker) encodes the old 24h guarantee. Severity-classifier to set final; expected QA/Low after owner-trust discount.

title: Consumer-side: does the global setAsideBufferRecipient (intended stable-staker) correctly absorb bare aggregated ERC20 inflows pooled from MULTIPLE clients? — cross-repo, ties to stable-staker M-05
severity-proposal: Out of in-scope econ surface — hand to story-faithfulness / interaction (no finding raised here)
economic-mechanism: story-047 sends the aggregate set-aside as a plain ERC20 safeTransfer with no callback and no strategy-level event (only the token Transfer; LOCAL-MKT-047-002). The recipient previously would have received only flows it initiated; it now receives unsolicited, batched inflows representing MULTIPLE clients' pooled set-asides. Whether the recipient (stable-staker) attributes/accounts these bare inflows correctly is a property of the consumer contract, which lives in a different repo and is outside run-15 scope.
who-loses: Potentially mis-accounted if the consumer cannot reconcile a bare inflow against per-client attribution (strategy emits only per-client SNAPSHOT SurplusSkimmed in vault-asset terms, which never equals the realized split).
preconditions: setAsideBufferRecipient set to stable-staker; nonzero buffers configured; skim executed.
relation-to-changed-code/ledger: story-047 trust boundary. Plausibly the integration leg of stable-staker M-05 (ledger ss7m5/0dca43f3, pro-rata-haircut redistribution). Cross-repo: verification of the consumer belongs to a stable-staker run / story-faithfulness, not this econ scan. Raised here only for Law-1 visibility and to ensure the interaction question is not dropped. Recommend the strategy emit a BufferSetAside(recipient, totalSetAside, toRecipient) event to make the recipient-vs-buffer split reconstructable off-chain (LOCAL-MKT-047-002).
